question.text: At <math><msup><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> , nitrogen exists as <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> and phosphorous exists as <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> because

options.text: <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  has valence electrons only in bonding and nonbonding orbitals, while P has valence electrons in both bonding and antibonding orbitals
higher electronegativity of N favours formation of multiple bonds
bigger size of P does not favour multiple bonds
P has preference to adapt structures with small bond angles

solution.text: Due to larger atomic size <math> <mtext>P</mtext></math> is unable to form pi bond and so it is tetra-atomic <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> in which each <math> <mtext>P</mtext></math> atom is linked with <math> <mtext>3</mtext></math> other <math> <mtext>P</mtext></math> atoms by <math> <mtext>3</mtext></math> sigma bonds. But, due to smaller atomic size <math> <mtext>N</mtext></math> forms <math> <mtext>1</mtext></math> sigma and <math> <mtext>2</mtext></math> pi bonds i.e. triple bonds with other <math> <mtext>N</mtext></math> atom and exists as diatomic molecule <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> .
